project: A Subject-Independent KAN-Based Framework for Non-Contact Heart-Rate Estimation from 120-GHz FMCW Radar Signals
stage: Phase 3 — Scientific Preflight and Dataset Readiness

user_approved_decisions.approval_scope: Approved for proceeding under the documented synchronization assumptions and limitations.
retained_assumptions_and_limitations: Hardware clock synchronization remains UNVERIFIED (no PPS pulses, TTL trigger signals, or common digitizer clock timestamps found in any of the 96 files).
Relative timing alignment relies on the nominal zero-offset assumption (t0 = 0.0 s for both radar and reference devices).
Mindray monitor display HR array remains strictly DISQUALIFIED from serving as supervised training labels due to the documented +6s to +7s display delay.
This approval constitutes an operational user decision to proceed with window-level evaluation, NOT independent physical or mathematical proof of sub-second hardware synchronization.

user_approved_decisions.topic: ECG R-Peak Detection and Quality-Screening Approach
user_approved_decisions.approval_scope: Approved for proceeding using the documented proposed SQI screening criteria.
retained_assumptions_and_limitations: In-memory linear interpolation of isolated periodic delimiter NaNs is authorized strictly for continuous QRS detection; zero raw MAT files are modified.
VS20_Apnea exhibited a reported maximum RR gap of 3.12 s and does not meet the proposed maximum-gap criterion (< 3.0 s).
VS10_Resting exhibits a delimiter NaN at sample index 0 (leading boundary), requiring explicit documented handling.
Recordings or windows failing the SQI criteria are strictly excluded from supervised ground-truth label generation.
A passing SQI score validates ECG physiological plausibility, but does NOT prove physical synchronization with the radar signal.
This approval constitutes an operational user decision on quality screening thresholds, NOT proof that every raw ECG recording in the dataset is free of artifacts.

user_approved_decisions.approved_filter: Cardiac 0.8–3.0 Hz Bandpass Filter (3rd-order zero-phase Butterworth, 48–180 bpm)

empirical_basis.nyquist_validity: Valid across all 48 recordings (high cutoff 3.0 Hz << 166.67 Hz Nyquist)

retained_assumptions_and_limitations: Selection of 0.8–3.0 Hz filter is based strictly on empirical cardiac-band power concentration.
Cardiac-band power concentration is explicitly distinguished from downstream heart-rate estimation accuracy.
No claim is made that this filter improves KAN or baseline model accuracy without empirical downstream model evaluation evidence.

governance_stop_condition.rule: Approval of Phase 3 preflight decisions does NOT automatically close the Phase 2A Finalization Gate or authorize persistent supervised label generation.
